title: The Transient Counting Statistics of Autonomous Quantum Clocks
abstract: At the heart of every atomic clock is a quantum coherent emitter, the laser, that could in principle be treated autonomously. While their frequency or phase stability is typically studied in the semiclassical regime of a large number of emitted quanta, recent works on autonomous quantum clocks suggest that the few-quanta regime can offer statistical information in the temporal domain. This provides complementary means to probe the fundamental limits to precise timekeeping in the quantum regime. Motivated by these works, we consider simple models for two- and three-level quantum emitters subject to an athermal fueling through dephasing, which generically results in coherences in the steady state. A large deviation principle with finite-time contributions is used to identify the transient counting statistics and their dependence on the initial conditions. We conclude by discussing the implications for precise timekeeping and quantum sensing using autonomous quantum emitters as clocks in their transient regime.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to analyze the transient counting statistics of autonomous quantum clocks modeled by multi-level emitters. By employing a revised Large Deviation Principle, the authors quantify how initial conditions affect the count statistics in the few-quanta regime. This provides a new, complementary tool for understanding the fundamental limits of precision timekeeping in quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses characterizing the fundamental limits to precise timekeeping and quantum sensing using autonomous quantum emitters when operating in the few-quanta regime.
main_result: It develops a framework to characterize transient initial-state contributions to the counting statistics, providing complementary insights beyond the standard semiclassical or steady-state analyses.
method: The analysis employs a revised Large Deviation Principle incorporating finite-time contributions, utilizing the moment generating function (MGF) derived from the evolution of the tilted density operator.
model_or_system: The system models simple two- and three-level quantum emitters (lasers) acting as quantum coherent emitters, whose dynamics are governed by the Lindblad master equation and fueled by dephasing quantum noise.
key_observables: Transient counting statistics, average number of jumps $\langle N angle_t$, and the variance of the count record.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the few-quanta regime ($\langle N angle_t \sim 1$) in the temporal domain, contrasting with the semiclassical regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the use of radiative transitions in an artificial atom and develops a framework to retain transient initial-state contributions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates clock dynamics for both two-level and three-level emitters, detailing the decay and dephasing pumping mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general framework of quantum emitter dynamics (Lindblad equation) to applying advanced statistical tools (LDP, MGF) to calculate transient counting statistics, culminating in discussions on timekeeping implications.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics, specifically quantum optics and open quantum systems, as it pushes the theoretical understanding of quantum measurement statistics into the non-trivial transient regime.
